construct: RULED, THE K2 CELL (refreshed 2026-09-21): k2_overview 40–70w (the persona's current in the element's arena) + k2_functional ≤22w (the god's own family function, re-ruled 2026-09-01) + k2_domain_readings 18–55w per ruled domain (owner construct 2026-08-19, corpus ×50 LOCKED) · adj_chips {catalyst ×3, friction ×3} 1–3w under THE KEYWORD DERIVATION CHAIN (2026-09-03) and THE VOCABULARY ZONE B1–B2 (2026-09-04) · fn_reading = the weighted three-door ledger {word, doors:{trait, scene, outside}} ×3 per pole, 35–55w per door (THE THREE DOORS 2026-09-03; corpus ×50 complete 2026-09-04) · structural_interaction = the REA_03 §4b authoring seed · k2_card = the unauthored register stub (REA_03 §4, superseded by the cell above). Prompts: REA_17 §3.4. · edge (catalyst pole only; owner 2026-10-16, THE EDGE v9: two sentences, the energy and its three ruling domains from the GOD table, then a clause per domain in The Pattern's voice; the metric; the head derived in the app)

candidates.structural_interaction: Stability meeting stability cross-polarity — ground competing with ground
candidates.k2_overview: Your Earth moves as the Rival: ground that expands by wager. You bet acreage where others bet coins, patient about the campaign, bold about the claim. Shared land, family stakes, and joint holdings follow you through life. You win them by daring and keep them by the paperwork you almost skipped.
candidates.k2_functional: Your energy is heavy machinery: slow to start, formidable engaged, needing scheduled idle.

k2_domain_readings.Rivalry: Your rivalries are territorial and patient: the competing shop, the sibling’s acreage, the slow contest of estates. Compete by building better rather than holding harder. Ground won by improvement stays won.
k2_domain_readings.Shared stakes: Everything significant you own will at some point be co-owned: family land, joint ventures, marriages of assets. Survey early, deed clearly, and revisit the map annually. Your fortune lives in shared soil.
k2_domain_readings.Boldness: Your daring moves mountains occasionally: the land bought unseen, the advantage taken calmly. Because your bets are heavy, space them. Earth recovers slowly from the ones that slide.

angles.drive: You are better with a rival in sight. Your own pace never quite wakes you, so you measure yourself against a person rather than a plan. Pick your rivals on purpose, and you turn a reflex into the fastest way you grow.
angles.cost_self: Being better with rivals leaves you rarely at your best alone. Without someone to beat, you drift rather than push, so the goals only you care about wait longest. Find a rival for the private goals too, and you stop leaving your own for last.
angles.cost_others: Better with a rival, you turn a peer into one without asking. You would rather race someone than keep them company, and you hand a contest to a friend who wanted none. Name the race, and you give them the choice to run it.

angles.drive: You bet big because only a real stake gets all of you, and you would rather risk a lot on one move than a little on many. If you let small bets count too, you stop missing the gains that come slowly.
angles.cost_self: Where you bet big, you lose at the same size. You stake the whole amount instead of keeping some in reserve. When you hold back one part of each bet, you keep the savings a single loss would take.
angles.cost_others: On a shared stake, you bet someone else's year with your own. You would rather win it all for both of you than keep half safe, and their caution becomes your dare. Ask first, because you keep a partner who chose the risk.

angles.drive: With a win in hand, you would rather share the credit than keep it, because a prize means more with your people inside it. When a win can count before you have shared it, you get to enjoy it twice.
angles.cost_self: Taking the credit alone feels like showing off to you. You hand out credit rather than keep it, and your own work goes unnamed. If you put your own name on your part, you stop losing the chances that follow credit.
angles.cost_others: The credit you share lands on people who did not run for it. You would rather have company at the finish than stand there alone, and you pass out what only you earned. Name who did what, to give praise each person can use.

angles.drive: In new company, you are comparing before you have said much. A clear rank makes you feel safe, and you compare yourself to someone rather than get to know them. You wanted a place among them, and ranking felt like the quick way in.
angles.cost_self: Always comparing gives you a result and never rest. You would rather know where you rank than enjoy where you are, so no win gets time to feel like one. You lose the quiet of a good week to a score you keep alone.
angles.cost_others: Whenever a friend has good news, you compare before you say well done. You measure the gap ahead of being glad for them, and you give less praise than they earned. You take some of the joy out of the news they bring you.

angles.drive: You feel every loss as a blow to your standing. You would rather sit out a contest than risk losing it, because your standing feels at stake. You carry each loss for weeks after the contest itself is over.
angles.cost_self: Hating to lose costs you the losses that would have taught you most. You would rather not play than be beaten, and you never enter the contests with the most to teach you. You protect a record with very few wins on it.
angles.cost_others: Shared things turn into contests when you hate to lose. You would rather win the argument than keep the evening, and you turn an easy talk with a friend into a match. You leave with the point and a little less warmth.

angles.drive: As a contest gets close, you spend to win it. You would rather pay to stay ahead than risk falling behind, and you spend to prove a point. Ask yourself before you pay whether you want the thing or only the win.
angles.cost_self: Where you spend to win, you end up with the win and without the money. You would rather look ahead of a rival than quietly stay ahead, so the savings go on rounds nobody asked for. You count the cost when the account runs dry.
angles.cost_others: To win, you spend what is not only yours. You would rather cover the whole bill than split it, and you spend money your partner set aside for the two of you. Along with the money, you spend a plan you made together.

edge.lead: Earth runs through your wealth, your social life and your career. It is the deal you win by asking again, the race that makes a friend of the one you beat, and the seat at work you took before anyone offered it.
